Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female presenting with 3 days of dysuria and mild lower abdominal discomfort, likely due to a urinary tract infection; antibiotics prescribed, with follow-up advised if symptoms worsen or do not resolve.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painful urination (“stinging”), ongoing for a few days.
- Timeline: Symptoms started ~3 days ago; not improving.
- Nature of pain: Stinging on urination, mild lower abdominal pain described as “kind of cramping” but distinct from menstrual cramps.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Brief episode of visible blood in urine earlier today.
  - Foul-smelling urine.
  - No increased urinary frequency noted.
  - No nausea, vomiting, fever, or back/flank pain.
  - No abnormal vaginal discharge.
- Bowel function: Normal; no diarrhea or loose stool.
- Menstrual history: Last period approximately 3 weeks ago.
- Sexual history: Sexually active with regular boyfriend of 2 months; uses condoms; no prior STD screen; reports low risk for pregnancy.
- Pertinent negatives: No systemic symptoms (no fever, nausea, vomiting, or back pain).

Past Medical History:
- Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS); no current symptoms or complications mentioned.
- Allergies: Clindamycin (causes swelling; severity described as “quite severe”).
- Medications: 
  - Tried over-the-counter bicarbonate (dose/route/frequency not documented) a few days ago, without benefit.
  - No regular medications.

Social History:
- Lives in a flat near college with friends; not living with family.
- College student studying biology.
- Denies smoking.
- Drinks alcohol socially on weekends.

Family History:
- No known family history of renal, bladder, bowel, or gastrointestinal disease.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed/documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations, imaging, or tests documented.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1: Urinary Tract Infection (likely cystitis)
  - Assessment: 3 days of dysuria, minor visible hematuria, lower abdominal discomfort, malodorous urine, no systemic symptoms; consistent with uncomplicated UTI.
  - Plan:
    - Empiric antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim (specific drug and dose/route/frequency not definitively chosen; doctor suggested “one tablet, twice a day, for three days”).
    - Advise increased oral fluid intake.
    - Cranberry juice may be beneficial for symptoms.
    - Avoid sexual intercourse until symptoms have fully resolved.
    - Continue to use barrier contraception.
    - Safety net: If symptoms worsen (fever, back pain, systemic illness), or do not resolve after antibiotics, return for reassessment.
    - Consider pregnancy test if any suspicion arises.

General plan items:
  - None noted outside above.

Quality checks:

● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs or physical examination findings documented.
  - No urinalysis or urine culture performed/documented.
  - No medication reconciliation beyond what is explicitly stated.
  - No explicit inquiry regarding full medication list or other allergies.
  - No formal past surgical history.

● Internal conflicts:
  - None identified.

● Transcript quality:
  - Good; minimal extraneous content. All pertinent clinical details clearly elicited.
